q: Why are fuels such as natural gas burned in homes and power stations?
options: Combustion is endothermic and takes in thermal energy from the surroundings.
Combustion is exothermic and takes in thermal energy from the surroundings.
Combustion is endothermic and transfers thermal energy to the surroundings.
Combustion is exothermic and transfers thermal energy to the surroundings.
explain: Fuels are useful because burning them releases large amounts of thermal energy.

q: Which statement about reaction pathway diagrams is correct?
options: The horizontal axis shows the energy of the particles.
The products are always drawn lower than the reactants.
The height of the peak shows the temperature of the reaction.
The difference in height between the reactants and the products shows the energy transferred in the reaction.
explain: The vertical gap between the reactants and the products levels gives the energy released or absorbed.

q: Which statement explains why a reaction is exothermic in terms of bonds?
options: More energy is released when bonds form in the products than is needed to break the bonds in the reactants.
The bonds in the reactants are broken without any energy being needed.
The number of bonds broken is always greater than the number of bonds made.
More energy is needed to break the bonds in the reactants than is released when bonds form in the products.
explain: If bond making releases more than bond breaking takes in, there is a net release of energy.

q: A reaction pathway diagram for a reaction shows that the products are at a lower energy than the reactants. Which of these observations would also be seen?
options: The thermometer reading in the reaction mixture increases.
The thermometer reading in the reaction mixture decreases.
The reaction stops when heating is stopped.
The mass of the reaction mixture decreases.
explain: A lower energy for the products means energy is released as heat, so the temperature goes up.

q: For the reaction 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g), ΔH = −486 kJ/mol. How much thermal energy is released when 1 mol of hydrogen gas burns in excess oxygen?
options: 243 kJ
972 kJ
486 kJ
explain: The equation uses 2 mol of H₂ for 486 kJ released, so 1 mol releases 486 ÷ 2 = 243 kJ.

q: In a reaction pathway diagram, the energy of the products is lower than the energy of the reactants. Which statement is correct?
options: The reaction takes in thermal energy from the surroundings.
The reaction is exothermic.
The reaction is endothermic.
The temperature of the surroundings decreases.
explain: Products at a lower energy level means that energy was released to the surroundings.

q: A student adds 2.0 g of a solid to water. The temperature of the water falls from 25.0 °C to 19.5 °C. What is the correct conclusion?
options: The dissolving is exothermic, and the temperature rose by 5.5 °C.
The dissolving is endothermic, and the temperature rose by 5.5 °C.
The dissolving is exothermic, and the temperature fell by 5.5 °C.
The dissolving is endothermic, and the temperature fell by 5.5 °C.
explain: 25.0 − 19.5 = 5.5 °C fall in temperature, so thermal energy was taken in from the water.

q: Why is a polystyrene cup with a lid used when measuring the temperature change of a reaction in solution?
options: to stop the reactants from reacting with the air
to reduce the transfer of thermal energy between the mixture and the surroundings
to make the reaction exothermic
to increase the amount of thermal energy released by the reaction
explain: Polystyrene is a good insulator, so less energy is lost to or gained from the room and the temperature change is measured more accurately.

q: Which bonds are broken in the reaction C₂H₄(g) + H₂(g) → C₂H₆(g)?
options: one C–C bond and one H–H bond
one C=C bond and two C–H bonds
four C–H bonds and one H–H bond
one C=C bond (becoming C–C) and one H–H bond
explain: Hydrogenation breaks the H–H bond and one of the two bonds in C=C; the bond left is C–C and two new C–H bonds form.

q: Magnesium is added to dilute hydrochloric acid. The temperature of the mixture rises from 20 °C to 31 °C. What is the correct description of the reaction?
options: Endothermic, because thermal energy is transferred to the surroundings.
Endothermic, because the temperature of the mixture increases.
Exothermic, because thermal energy is transferred to the surroundings.
Exothermic, because thermal energy is taken in from the surroundings.
explain: A temperature rise shows that thermal energy is given out, which is the definition of exothermic.

q: In a reaction pathway diagram, the energy of the products is higher than the energy of the reactants. Which statement is correct?
options: The reaction is exothermic.
The reaction is endothermic.
The temperature of the surroundings increases.
The reaction releases thermal energy to the surroundings.
explain: When products are at a higher energy level than reactants, energy has been taken in from the surroundings.

q: Use the bond energies (H–H 436, Cl–Cl 243, H–Cl 432, all in kJ/mol) to calculate ΔH for 2HCl(g) → H₂(g) + Cl₂(g).
options: −185 kJ/mol
+185 kJ/mol
−864 kJ/mol
+1543 kJ/mol
explain: Broken: 2 × 432 = 864. Made: 436 + 243 = 679. ΔH = 864 − 679 = +185 kJ/mol, so the reaction is endothermic.

q: A reaction has ΔH = +92 kJ/mol. Which description is correct?
options: The reaction is exothermic and the surroundings become colder.
The reaction is endothermic and the surroundings become warmer.
The reaction is exothermic and the surroundings become warmer.
The reaction is endothermic and the surroundings become colder.
explain: A positive ΔH shows that thermal energy is taken in from the surroundings, which cool.

q: Use the bond energies (H–H 436, O=O 498, O–H 464, all in kJ/mol) to calculate ΔH for 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g).
options: −486 kJ/mol
+486 kJ/mol
−1370 kJ/mol
−1856 kJ/mol

q: A student increases the temperature of a reaction. What happens to the activation energy of the reaction?
options: It decreases.
It stays the same.
It becomes equal to ΔH.
It increases.
explain: Activation energy depends on the reaction pathway; a higher temperature just means more particles have energy greater than Ea.

q: For H₂(g) + ½O₂(g) → H₂O(g), what is ΔH given that ΔH for 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(g) is −486 kJ/mol?
options: −486 kJ/mol
−243 kJ/mol
+243 kJ/mol
−972 kJ/mol
explain: The equation is halved so ΔH is halved: −486 ÷ 2 = −243 kJ/mol.

q: A student mixes citric acid solution with sodium hydrogencarbonate. Bubbles are seen and the temperature falls by 6 °C. Which statement is correct?
options: Energy is transferred from the reaction to the surroundings.
The reaction is neither endothermic nor exothermic.
The reaction is endothermic.
The reaction is exothermic.
explain: A fall in temperature means energy is absorbed from the surroundings.

q: The enthalpy change for H₂(g) + F₂(g) → 2HF(g) is −542 kJ/mol. The bond energies are H–H 436 kJ/mol and F–F 158 kJ/mol. What is the bond energy of H–F?
options: 568 kJ/mol
284 kJ/mol
26 kJ/mol
1136 kJ/mol

q: A reaction pathway diagram shows reactants at 200 kJ/mol, a peak at 350 kJ/mol and products at 120 kJ/mol. What are the values of ΔH and Ea?
options: ΔH = +80 kJ/mol | Ea = +150 kJ/mol
ΔH = −80 kJ/mol | Ea = +230 kJ/mol
ΔH = −150 kJ/mol | Ea = +80 kJ/mol
ΔH = −80 kJ/mol | Ea = +150 kJ/mol

q: A reaction pathway diagram shows reactants at 100 kJ/mol, a peak at 250 kJ/mol and products at 40 kJ/mol. What is the activation energy for the reverse reaction?
options: 60 kJ/mol
150 kJ/mol
210 kJ/mol
290 kJ/mol
explain: The reverse reaction starts at the products level (40) and must climb to the peak (250): 250 − 40 = 210 kJ/mol.

q: Magnesium burns in air with a bright white flame to form magnesium oxide. Which statement about the energy change is correct?
options: Thermal energy (and light) is released, so the reaction is exothermic.
Light is released, so the reaction is endothermic.
Thermal energy is absorbed, so the reaction is endothermic.
No energy is transferred because a solid is formed.
explain: Burning in air gives out heat and light, so the reaction is exothermic.

q: Which row correctly describes the thermal decomposition of calcium carbonate?
options: exothermic | transferred to surroundings | surroundings become cooler
endothermic | transferred to surroundings | surroundings become warmer
endothermic | taken in from surroundings | surroundings become cooler
exothermic | taken in from surroundings | surroundings become cooler
explain: Decomposing calcium carbonate needs heat to be supplied, so energy is taken in and the surroundings cool.

q: In a reaction, the total energy needed to break all the bonds in the reactants is 2800 kJ/mol and the total energy released when the bonds in the products form is 3300 kJ/mol. What is ΔH and what type of reaction is it?
options: ΔH = −500 kJ/mol; endothermic
ΔH = +6100 kJ/mol; endothermic
ΔH = +500 kJ/mol; exothermic
ΔH = −500 kJ/mol; exothermic
explain: ΔH = 2800 − 3300 = −500 kJ/mol; a negative value means exothermic.

q: Which reaction mixture would you expect to get colder as the reaction proceeds?
options: dilute sulfuric acid added to sodium hydroxide solution
sodium metal added to water
iron wool burning in oxygen
solid barium hydroxide and solid ammonium thiocyanate being stirred together
explain: The reaction between barium hydroxide and ammonium thiocyanate is strongly endothermic, so the flask becomes very cold.

q: What is the name given to the transfer of thermal energy during a chemical reaction?
options: specific heat capacity
bond energy
activation energy, Ea
enthalpy change, ΔH
explain: ΔH is the symbol for the enthalpy change, the thermal energy transferred in a reaction.

q: Which expression gives the enthalpy change of a reaction using bond energies?
options: ΔH = energy needed to break bonds + energy released when bonds form
ΔH = energy released when bonds form − energy needed to break bonds
ΔH = energy needed to break bonds − energy released when bonds form
ΔH = energy of the products ÷ energy of the reactants
explain: Breaking bonds is endothermic (+) and making bonds is exothermic (−), so ΔH = broken − made.

q: Nitrogen gas is very unreactive at room temperature, even though many of its reactions are exothermic. What is the best explanation?
options: The strong N≡N triple bond gives a very high activation energy.
The N≡N bond is so weak that it breaks again immediately.
All reactions of nitrogen are endothermic.
Nitrogen reactions have a ΔH of zero.
explain: Large amounts of energy are needed to break the strong triple bond, so few collisions are energetic enough.

q: A student claims, "Burning is endothermic because a match must be used to start it." Why is the student wrong?
options: Overall, burning transfers thermal energy to the surroundings, so it is exothermic.
Overall, burning transfers thermal energy to the surroundings, so it is endothermic.
Overall, burning takes in thermal energy from the surroundings, so it is exothermic.
Overall, burning takes in thermal energy from the surroundings, so it is endothermic.
explain: The match only starts the reaction; once going, burning releases far more energy than it needs.

q: Use the bond energies (H–H 436, I–I 151, H–I 299, all in kJ/mol) to calculate ΔH for H₂(g) + I₂(g) → 2HI(g).
options: +11 kJ/mol
−598 kJ/mol
−11 kJ/mol
−587 kJ/mol

q: Which pair of substances would give an increase in temperature when mixed in a beaker?
options: solid ammonium nitrate and water
citric acid solution and sodium hydrogencarbonate
sodium hydroxide solution and dilute hydrochloric acid
solid ammonium chloride and water
explain: Neutralisation is exothermic; the other three mixtures all cool down.
